task: Close the two blockers an independent NEW CHAT review of commit 1d52ec1 established (BLOCKED_BY_SOURCE_OBJECT_PROVENANCE, BLOCKED_BY_INVALID_INPUT_HANDLING) by adding a narrow, strategy-independent DailyMarketEvidenceV1 record-assembly boundary. Does not touch OHLC, duplicate, timestamp, or event-order logic in either parser.

frozen_protocol_binding.note: all three re-verified byte-identical before and after this task; this task modifies no frozen protocol artifact, only adds new implementation/test/receipt files

parser_hashes.note: identical to the post-1d52ec1 hashes verified in the prior independent review; this task made zero edits to qntylab/r1_reference_parser.py or qntylab/r1_retention_candidate.py

record_validator_location: validate_daily_market_evidence_v1 lives in the same module as the assemblers (qntylab/r1_daily_market_materializer.py); no separate module/hash

protocol_underspecification_check.question: Does closing the uncaught-exception gap require inventing a new contract-visible status?
protocol_underspecification_check.finding: No. qntylab.r1_retention_candidate.ANOMALY_CONTAINER ("CONTAINER_ANOMALY") is already declared and already listed in experiments/data/r1_bounded_evidence_retention_candidate_v1.json:anomaly_triggers, but was never wired to any raising code path before this task. This task activates that already-declared-but-dormant trigger; it does not introduce a new name.
protocol_underspecification_check.instrument_instance_id_naming_note: qntylab.r1_retention_candidate.daily_primitive's own dict key is stream_id (its internal candidate parameter name), not the contract's instrument_instance_id. The boundary performs a pure rename (record['instrument_instance_id'] = record.pop('stream_id')) when assembling Parser B's record; this is not a scientific decision and changes no computed value.
protocol_underspecification_check.outcome: not blocked; no new protocol invented

source_object_sha256_binding_rule.parser_a_path: parse_daily_object already embeds source_object_sha256; the boundary independently recomputes sha256(raw_bytes) and requires exact equality before accepting the record, failing closed (ANOMALY_SOURCE_MUTATION) on any mismatch
source_object_sha256_binding_rule.parser_b_path: daily_primitive never receives raw bytes and never computes this field; the boundary computes sha256(raw_bytes) exactly once and binds it into the assembled record; normalized_primitive_sha256 (a hash of the primitive dict) is never reused for this field -- they are different quantities over different inputs
source_object_sha256_binding_rule.missingness_rule_applied: per r1_normalized_evidence_contract_v1.json's own text ("never null for a day with trade_count>0; null only when trade_count=0 and no object was retrievable"), source_object_sha256 is bound in every record this boundary emits, independent of trade_count, because the boundary is only ever invoked with raw bytes already in hand -- the object was always retrievable from its point of view
source_object_sha256_binding_rule.exact_byte_binding_verified: row-permutation counterfactual test confirms canonical derived fields (open/close/base_volume/quote_turnover/trade_count) are unchanged while source_object_sha256 differs between byte-different, logically-equal raw objects, for both parser paths

typed_malformed_object_rule.gzip_corruption: non-gzip / corrupt-container bytes now produce a typed MATERIALIZATION_QUARANTINED_NO_RECORD result with anomaly CONTAINER_ANOMALY, for both parser paths, instead of an uncaught GzipCorruptionError
typed_malformed_object_rule.truncated_csv: gzip-valid but structurally truncated CSV (e.g. a single-column header) now produces the same typed quarantine result instead of an uncaught TruncatedCSVError, for both parser paths
typed_malformed_object_rule.empty_object: zero-byte raw bytes and gzip-valid-empty-body both remain a typed MATERIALIZED_VALID_RECORD with trade_count=0 (unchanged, pre-existing typed behavior; source_object_sha256 now correctly bound even in this case)
typed_malformed_object_rule.malformed_row: unchanged pre-existing typed PARSE_REJECTION accounting (rejected_row_count), not altered by this task

batch_isolation_rule.primitive: materialize_batch(items, materialize_fn) calls materialize_fn once per item and appends its MaterializationResult; no exception from a single item can escape because materialize_parser_a/materialize_parser_b already convert every container-level exception into a typed result before returning
batch_isolation_rule.verified: valid/corrupt/valid batch fixture (both parser paths): the corrupt middle object is quarantined and the following valid object is still attempted and produces a correct record; valid_count + quarantined_count == len(items) with no unaccounted remainder

known_out_of_scope_findings_still_open.unknown_schema_ab_divergence: Parser A's parse_daily_object returns record=None (total quarantine) for an unregistered column set; Parser B's daily_primitive still computes and returns a populated core record with schema_id=None and a SCHEMA_MISMATCH anomaly for the same input. Not exercised by any of the 5 real cached objects (all have a known schema, zero anomalies) and not one of this task's two named blockers -- observed but explicitly not repaired here, per 'do not broaden the repair after a blocker'.
known_out_of_scope_findings_still_open.receipt_precision_overclaim: an earlier receipt (r1_timestamp_canonicalization_repair_v1.json) states source precision 'observed up to 4-6 digits'; independent token scan of all 5 real objects found a maximum of 4 fractional digits. Not corrected here (out of this task's scope; noted in the prior review).
